YOUR RESUME REVIEW

THE READ

CLARITY SUMMARY: 58/100

Not a prediction of interviews or offers.

Quantify sales ownership

Clear sales progression, but most bullets lack measurable commercial results.

WHAT LANDS

The sequence from Junior Sales Associate through Sales Executive gives recruiters a visible three-role progression from administrative support toward client and campaign work.

WHERE DOUBT CREEPS IN

The resume does not show quota, revenue, pipeline, win rate, deal size, or account volume, leaving your commercial level difficult to place.

FIX FIRST

Add [account count], [proposal volume], and [measurable result] to the BrightWave client-account bullet.

OTHER LINE REWRITES

Useful edits, kept with their own source.

These do not map uniquely to the ranked fixes above, so each stays beside the exact line it rewrites.

LINE EDIT 01 · SOURCE LINE

“- Helped prepare sales materials and participated in calls with prospective clients to present product features”

REWRITE

Helped prepare sales materials and participated in prospective-client calls to present product features; calls: [number]; result: [measurable result]

Add call volume and the verified result of those conversations to distinguish preparation from selling activity.

QUESTIONS WORTH ANSWERING

Prompts for your next revision.

These questions are not tied to a specific ranked fix. Use whichever ones surface a true, useful detail.

QUESTION 01

What changed in your responsibilities when you moved from Junior Sales Associate to Sales Representative?

Why it may help: The titles show progression, while the bullets use similar support language across roles.

QUESTION 02

How many client accounts, leads, proposals, or opportunities did you handle at BrightWave Solutions?

Why it may help: The resume mentions account management and lead generation but gives no workload scale.

QUESTION 03

Describe a difficult customer inquiry you handled and what happened afterward.

Why it may help: Customer communication appears in the role, but the level of difficulty and result are absent.

QUESTION 04

What changed after you contributed to customer engagement or sales strategy projects?

Why it may help: The project language suggests improvement work without identifying the before-and-after.

QUESTION 05

How did you coordinate marketing and sales outreach, and what did each team need from you?

Why it may help: The resume names coordination but not the competing requirements or your role in resolving them.

KEEP THESE

The parts already earning trust.
01

The sequence from Junior Sales Associate through Sales Executive gives recruiters a visible three-role progression from administrative support toward client and campaign work.

02

BrightWave includes both account activity and coordination between marketing and sales, which makes the experience broader than pure administrative support.

03

The resume shows repeated customer contact through meetings, calls, inquiries, appointments, and follow-up communications across all three employers.

ROLE DIRECTION

Where this story reads strongest.

Position yourself around the sales work you can verify, such as client accounts, lead generation, proposals, and cross-team outreach. Add commercial measures before targeting roles that expect independent quota ownership.

BEST FIT NOW

Sales Representative
Account Coordinator
Business Development Representative

Seniority read: The titles and four-plus years shown in the summary suggest early-career sales experience, but the page does not establish independent quota ownership.

report.biggest_gap_example: "- Helped manage client accounts and provided ongoing support to the sales team in developing proposals and presentations" is missing a measurable outcome, so we cannot place the impact.
report.first_impression: Your progression from Junior Sales Associate to Sales Executive is easy to follow, but nearly every bullet describes support rather than sales performance. The page names client work, lead generation, proposals, and CRM activity without showing pipeline, quota, revenue, or account results.
gaps: The resume does not show quota, revenue, pipeline, win rate, deal size, or account volume, leaving your commercial level difficult to place.
Your ownership remains unclear because many bullets use "helped," "supported," "assisted," or "contributed" without naming the decisions you made.
The three roles cover similar duties, but the resume does not explain how your responsibilities or customer-facing scope grew over time.

report.score_comment_long: The career progression and sales responsibilities are easy to scan. The bullets rarely include numbers, deal context, or measurable results, so the page reads more like a duty list than a performance record. Quantifying the BrightWave and Glenmark work is the fastest way to raise it.

report.score_plain: This resume can get you considered for support-oriented sales roles, but it will struggle against applicants showing quota, pipeline, and revenue results. Add verified sales measures to compete for independent selling roles.

BrightWave includes both account activity and coordination between marketing and sales, which makes the experience broader than pure administrative support.
The resume shows repeated customer contact through meetings, calls, inquiries, appointments, and follow-up communications across all three employers.
report.summary: Three sales roles from 2016 to 2023 show a steady move from event logistics and data entry into client accounts, lead generation, proposals, and marketing-sales coordination. Your page fits early-career sales or sales-support roles more clearly than an independent account executive role. The recurring pattern is customer contact plus team support, but no quota, pipeline, revenue, or account volume is attached to it. That leaves recruiters unsure how much of the sales cycle you personally owned.
